subject: Request: carve-out for customer-controlled infra & latency warranty — Rainbird Private deployment
messages:
From: Alan Kaplan <alan.kaplan@rainbird.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: RS Contracts <contracts@rainbird.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment SLA: carve-out request for network-controlled components

Ben —

Thanks again for the demo earlier this week. Our infra team has reviewed Redwood Private for the on-prem deployment and we have two outstanding concerns on SLA language that block procurement:

1) Latency warranty: Rainbird needs a binding latency commitment for 99th percentile tail latency for token-level inference when the model is served in our VPC. Our legal team has proposed 100ms 99p for text-generation in steady state.

2) Shared responsibility: because Rainbird will own the network, hardware, and load‑balancer configuration, we need clarity that any latency or downtime caused by customer-managed network devices (we have a complex east-west overlay) is excluded from Redwood's uptime/latency guarantees. Conversely, if the root cause traces to Redwood-managed software layers, we expect SLA remedies.

We attached a short network topology and a redline that Rainbird legal prepared. Can Redwood provide a redlined SLA that identifies the precise boundary and any monitoring/observability preconditions you require (sampling, agent, ping targets)? Procurement also asked about service credit mechanics if an exception is agreed.

Given timing, we'd like to get a decision on whether Redwood will accept a shared-responsibility carve-out (with defined monitoring gates) or propose an alternative tolerance within two business days. Happy to set a 30-minute call if that helps.

Thanks,

Alan Kaplan
Head of Cloud Operations — Rainbird Systems
alan.kaplan@rainbird.com
+1 (415) 555-0128

Attachments: rainbird_network_topology.pdf, RB_sla_redline_rainbird.docx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alan Kaplan <alan.kaplan@rainbird.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment SLA: carve-out request for network-controlled components

Alan —

Appreciate the clear ask and the topology diagram. Looping in Monica (customer reliability/CS) and Neha (legal) so we can respond with a concrete redline. A couple quick clarifications from our side so we scope the exception correctly:

- When you say "Rainbird will own the network," do you mean the entire L2/L3 overlay and on-prem load balancers (i.e., anything before the Redwood agent nodes in your VPC)?
- Do you have historical p95/p99 telemetry from the test runners you mentioned? If you can share p95/p99 for the month of Sep we can map expected delta.

High level proposal to move fast: we can prepare a redline that defines a split-SLA plus instrumentation conditions (agent heartbeat, span sampling, synthetic pings). If the root cause is within Redwood-managed processes (model-server, runtime, kv-cache), Redwood will make the SLA whole. If the root cause is in customer network appliances or underlying hardware outside the Redwood managed nodes, we’d exclude those events from uptime/latency calculations — but we’ll offer measurable remediation steps (runbooks, debug access, optional co-managed agent) during the trial period.

I'll aim to have a first-pass redline and a list of required observability checkpoints by Monday EOD. If Rainbird wants a sync, happy to do 30 minutes on Monday.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: none in this message

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 08:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment SLA: carve-out request for network-controlled components

Ben / team —

Technical summary for the redline (high level):

1) Scope boundary: Redwood will guarantee availability and latency for components under Redwood control: model-server processes, inference runtime, KV cache nodes that we ship as part of the Private package, and any orchestration primitives we manage via the Redwood agent. Anything upstream of the agent's NIC (customer LB, network appliances, ISP segments) is in the customer bucket.

2) Latency commitments: we can commit to p95 token latency targets in the base SLA (e.g., p95 < 50ms for small models on specified instances). For p99 we should move to a conditional warranty: Redwood will target p99 < 120ms when the following observability gates are met: agent heartbeat >= 99.5% over rolling 24h, TLS handshake < 30ms median from our synthetic probes, and customer peering egress latency < 30ms (measured from Redwood probes). If gates are not met, the p99 metric is excluded from SLA calculations and we treat incidents under shared responsibility.

3) Monitoring & evidence: require access to synthetic ping endpoints, syslogs, and a trimmed set of application traces for root cause analysis. We can offer an optional lightweight co-managed agent to provide deeper telemetry (installed by Rainbird).

4) Remedies: instead of a full availability credit for network-caused incidents, offer a graduated credit schedule for infra breaches triggered by Redwood-managed components. For shared-resp incidents we suggest a remediation obligation (runbook execution, joint RCA) but no monetary credit unless Redwood is shown to have misconfigured shipped artifacts.

Attached: latency-metrics-export.csv (sample of our lab run against similar topologies) and a docx with suggested redline bullets.

Happy to refine phrasing for legal.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com

Attachments: latency-metrics-export.csv, redwood_proposed_sla_redline_v1.docx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alan Kaplan <alan.kaplan@rainbird.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 14:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed compromise: conditional p99 warranty + trial & monitoring gates

Alan —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is a concise proposal (redline excerpt below) that attempts to meet Rainbird's need for a tail latency commitment while preserving a fair split for shared responsibility. High level:

- We’ll commit to 99.9% availability for Redwood-managed runtime components and a conditional p99 latency warranty for token-level inference (target 110ms).
- The p99 warranty is only measured when Rainbird meets the observability gates described (agent heartbeat, synthetic probe thresholds, and peering latency) for rolling 24h windows. When gates are not met, those windows are excluded from p99 calculations but we will run a joint RCA.
- During a 90-day trial period starting at first provisioning, Rainbird may opt into a co-managed agent to help validate gates; if the gates are met for 60 of 90 days, the full p99 warranty becomes active.
- Service credits: for qualifying Redwood-caused outages affecting availability, standard credit schedule applies (5% credit per 12h downtime, capped at 50% per month). For performance incidents that qualify under the active p99 warranty, we propose a single-tier credit equivalent to 2% monthly for each breached 24h measurement window, capped at 10%/month. No monetary credits for shared-resp incidents; instead, mutual remediation and RCA.

Action items:
1) Confirm you can provide historical p95/p99 telemetry for September (you mentioned test harness data).
2) Confirm acceptance of a 90-day trial with co-managed agent option.
3) Let us know if DocuSign is acceptable for quick execution — I can send the link.

I’ve included a DocuSign placeholder link here: https://www.docusign.com/placeholder/RB-SLA-374. If this approach works, Neha will produce a legal redline and I’ll route for signature.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_proposed_sla_redline_v1.docx, docusign_proposal_link.txt

From: Alan Kaplan <alan.kaplan@rainbird.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: RS Contracts <contracts@rainbird.com>, Procurement <procurement@rainbird.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Oct 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed compromise: conditional p99 warranty + trial & monitoring gates

Ben / team —

Thanks for the detailed proposal — the compromise looks reasonable and is close to what Rainbird legal will accept. A few quick asks before we greenlight:

- Add a small clause that explicitly allows Rainbird to declare a maintenance window for which Redwood will not seek credit, but also requires Redwood to provide a rollback plan and 2-hour escalation SLA during maintenance.
- Modify the trial acceptance condition: Rainbird requests 45 days of met gates (not 60) during the 90-day trial to trigger the p99 warranty. Our team can meet the co-managed agent install timeline.
- Add an explicit commitment that logs required for RCA will be retained for 90 days and accessible to Rainbird and Redwood for joint investigations.

Assuming those three edits, we can sign and proceed. Please send the DocuSign and we'll route it internally.

Alan Kaplan
Head of Cloud Operations — Rainbird Systems
alan.kaplan@rainbird.com

Attachments: signed_intent_placeholder.pdf (to follow DocuSign)
